A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DRIFT. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching content moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original AgentDojo experiments across five LLMs, component ablations, trajectory analyses and a case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds ASB evaluations, adaptive attacks, overhead measurements and additional comparative analyses.

M1.justification: The planner, validator, isolator, policy construction and LoRA training procedures remain unchanged. All six appendix prompts match after renumbering. Added evaluation clarifications and the Qwen Instruct designation do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds ASB's ten evaluation scenarios and adaptive injection scenarios while retaining AgentDojo's four domains and ToolBench-based training. The open-ended-task analysis reuses existing AgentDojo tasks rather than adding a dataset.

E2.justification: Progent changes from a cited concurrent approach to an evaluated dynamic-policy comparator on AgentDojo and ASB, including comparisons with two base models. The new ASB comparison includes delimiters_defense, ob_sandwich_defense and instructional_prevention; the original AgentDojo comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces adaptive-attack procedures, including PAIR optimization on previously defended cases, a manually selected six-task open-ended evaluation, and token-cost accounting with an efficiency metric. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original AgentDojo task counts and reported LoRA training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an isolator-only ablation, isolator/validator-targeted and PAIR stress tests, open-ended-task analysis, model-capability comparisons with Progent, and overhead analysis. The original cumulative ablations, trajectory analysis and hotel-booking case study are retained, with the case study moved to Appendix C.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges this absence without changing the point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original detailed AgentDojo values remain unchanged. v2 adds ASB results, including 4.8% DRIFT ASR versus 15.8% for Progent, an isolator-only ASR of 7.95%, and adaptive-attack, cost and open-ended-task results. However, Table 5 reports GPT-4o-mini DRIFT scores of 61.24/46.30/1.64 versus 58.48/47.91/1.29 in Tables 6–8 without explaining a setting difference; these cannot establish comparable performance gains. Section 3.2 also corrects the CaMeL ASR gap from 1.6 to 1.3 percentage points.

T1.justification: Section 3.7 newly defines efficiency as (Utility − ASR) / Total Tokens. This is a limited mathematical definition accompanying the cost metric; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims about dynamic control/data policies, memory isolation, security, utility and adaptability. Adding ASB broadens supporting evidence without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of adaptive-attack resilience, utility retention on open-ended tasks and computational trade-offs. Appendix C.2 attributes robustness relative to Progent on weaker models to simpler privilege and intent-checking subtasks. The original limitations and case-study interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 names default attacks, specifies Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and clarifies that user-approval requests count as rejected calls during evaluation. It announces code release at an updated repository and a future training-dataset release, but omits v1's 15,000-token maximum-input disclosure. These are documentation and access-information changes.

R1.justification: References for ASB, PAIR and several baseline defenses are added. The existing positioning against Progent gains a specific argument about simpler policy-update subtasks, while the related-work taxonomy and principal novelty rationale remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 edits the introduction and defense background, standardizes model names and updates author and venue information. Limitations and the case study move into appendices, and a conference checklist is added. Most existing method, training, related-work and conclusion prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ASB figure and four analytical tables, expands Figure 3 with Progent, and revises Table 1 to show explicit component combinations and an isolator-only row. Existing cross-model and trajectory figures remain; the hotel case-study figure moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v1's security and practicality claims lacked adaptive-adversary testing and cost evidence. v2 directly addresses these gaps and evaluates a competing dynamic defense across two benchmarks, substantially improving assessment of robustness and operational trade-offs. Table 5's unexplained AgentDojo discrepancies and missing uncertainty and attack-budget details limit precision, but the added evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
